snippet: return i < 0 ? 0 : i;                                 // an unknown level is NONE, never a
reason: PROVABLY EQUIVALENT. `i` is Array.indexOf, so its range is exactly {-1, 0, 1, 2, 3}. The guard maps -1 to 0 and returns i otherwise; under <= the only additional case is i === 0, which returns 0 — the same value it would have returned anyway. No input distinguishes the two, so no test can. Kept as a mutant rather than rewritten, because the guard reads correctly as written.

PROVABLY EQUIVALENT. Both sides were produced by grant(), which normalises every level through LEVELS[rank(lvl)] — so equal rank means an identical canonical string. Under >= the extra case is rank equality, which assigns parent's value over an already-identical child value. The assignment is a no-op, so the clamp cannot be observed to behave differently. The stricter > is kept because it says what is meant: only clamp when the child is actually asking for more.
